idiom_name: readonly discriminated-union nodes + readonly frame list + assertNever switch
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not runtime guarantees: model nodes and frames as readonly discriminated unions, navigate with a switch whose default arm passes the value to assertNever (so a new node kind is a compile error), and rebuild the parent with a map over the children. readonly is erased at runtime, so the immutability is a compile-time contract - freeze nodes or keep them private if other code can hold them. A generic typed protocol (branch/children/makeNode) can be written once for arrays, JSON and ASTs; for fixed paths a typed optic is simpler, and @thi.ng/zipper is the packaged library form.
pitfalls: readonly is a compile-time fiction: JSON.parse, an `as Node` cast or any plain JavaScript caller can hand over mutable nodes, so the guarantee must be re-established at every boundary.
A default arm that returns undefined instead of calling assertNever silently defeats exhaustiveness - the main reason to model the tree as a discriminated union in the first place.
Spreading a node copies one level and shares the children array, so a later in-place push is visible through both versions.
Structural typing makes two node types with the same shape interchangeable; if the kind field widens to string, narrowing stops working.

variants.name: @thi.ng/zipper Location with typed ZipperOps
variants.idiom_name: zipper(...) with ZipperOps<T> and a typed Location<T>
variants.implementation_notes: The typed packaged form: @thi.ng/zipper ships its own declarations, so Location<T> exposes node/path/children/depth/isBranch/isFirst/isLast accessors plus appendChild/insertChild/insertLeft/insertRight/remove/replace/update edits, described once through ZipperOps<T> (branch, children, factory) and zipped back with .root. Use it when the tree is JSON-like and the verbs are wanted as-is; keep the hand-rolled union when the node type is a domain AST whose operations must stay closed and exhaustively checked by the compiler.
pitfalls: ZipperOps must match the node representation exactly; a wrong branch/children pair makes navigation skip subtrees silently instead of failing.
Location values are immutable but partial chains are the norm - only .root materialises the new tree, so a chain must be finished or kept.
The package pulls in the wider @thi.ng/api dependency, which is two extra packages for a small amount of tree editing in a bundle-sensitive frontend.
